selected_problem: Fresh main persisted after.sha256/after.size/after.contentBase64 for each staged write, but apply decoded and wrote after.contentBase64 without checking that the persisted bytes still matched the staged postimage metadata. Corrupted durable changeset content could therefore produce a workspace state different from the postimage that the changeset itself claimed to apply.
decision_basis: The execution-kernel contract already defines after.sha256 and after.contentBase64 as the transactional postimage; enforcing their self-consistency closes an existing invariant rather than choosing a new architecture.
The verification happens before any workspace mutation and keeps delete semantics explicit, preserving fail-closed transactional behavior.
Hosted Developer Execution Runtime remained temporarily unavailable with HTTP 502, so this cycle uses DWAC_SOURCE_CONTRACT_REPLAY（DWAC 源码契约重放） and does not claim a hosted DWAC success receipt.

pre_fix_reality.source_observation: ChangesetStore.apply wrote decode(c.after.contentBase64) directly while c.after.sha256 and c.after.size were only recorded metadata.
pre_fix_reality.impact: persisted staged bytes could diverge from their recorded postimage before apply

change: Apply now materializes and verifies each staged postimage before workspace preflight: write bytes must match recorded size and sha256, while delete postimages must remain null/zero. The verified bytes are the exact bytes later written.

validation.node_check: PASS on the exact proposed core/changesets.mjs content
validation.focused_changeset_replay: PASS: tampered persisted write content is rejected with CHANGESET_POSTIMAGE_CORRUPT before file creation; an intact staged write still reaches APPLIED and writes the expected bytes

truth_boundary: This verifies staged postimage self-consistency against its recorded hash/size. It is not an authenticated runtime-artifact signature and does not yet verify rollback preimage bytes before restoration.
